translations.literal: 1.2.1 Son Zhonghui
translations.idiomatic: 1.2.1 — Zhonghui

sentences.zh: 劉彥宗

translations.literal: Liu Yanzong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzong

sentences.zh: 劉彥宗，子魯開，大興宛平人。

translations.literal: Liu Yanzong, courtesy name Lukai, was a native of Wanping in Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzong, whose courtesy name was Lukai, came from Wanping in Daxing.

sentences.zh: 遠祖怦，唐盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: A distant ancestor, Bing, was military commissioner of Lulong under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His distant ancestor Bing had served as Tang military commissioner of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 石晉以幽、薊入遼，劉氏六世仕遼，相繼為宰相。

translations.literal: When the Later Jin ceded You and Ji to Liao, the Liu clan served Liao for six generations, succeeding one another as grand chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: After the Later Jin ceded Youzhou and Jizhou to the Liao, the Liu family served the Liao for six generations in a row as grand chancellors.

sentences.zh: 父霄，至中京留守。

translations.literal: His father Xiao rose to be resident commissioner of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiao eventually became resident commissioner of the Liao Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 彥宗擢進士乙科。

translations.literal: Yanzong passed the second rank of the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong placed in the second tier of the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 天祚走天德，秦晉國王耶律捏裏自立于燕，擢彥宗留守判官。

translations.literal: When Tianzuo fled to Tiande, the King of Qin and Jin, Yelü Nieli, declared himself ruler at Yan and promoted Yanzong to be an assistant to the resident commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tianzuo fled to Tiande, Yelü Nieli, king of Qin and Jin, set himself up at Yan and appointed Yanzong assistant to the resident commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蕭妃攝政，遷簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiao held regency, he was transferred to sign documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Xiao's regency he was moved to the post of signing clerk for the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太祖至居庸關，蕭妃自古北口遁去，都監高六送款于太祖。

translations.literal: When Taizu reached Juyong Pass, Empress Xiao fled through the Old Northern Pass; the commandant Gao Liu surrendered to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu reached Juyong Pass, Empress Xiao slipped away through the Old Northern Pass while Commandant Gao Liu offered his submission to the Jin founder.

sentences.zh: 太祖奄至，駐蹕城南，彥宗與左企弓等奉表降。

translations.literal: Taizu arrived suddenly, halted his imperial progress south of the city, and Yanzong together with Zuo Qigong and others presented a memorial of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder arrived without warning and made camp south of the city; Yanzong joined Zuo Qigong and others in presenting a formal surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖一見，器遇之，俾復舊，遷左僕射，佩金牌。

translations.literal: At their first meeting Taizu valued him highly, allowed him to resume his former standing, promoted him to Left Vice Director, and awarded him a gold plaque.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took to him at once, restored his former status, appointed him Left Vice Director, and bestowed a gold tablet of authority.

sentences.zh: 張覺為南京留守，太祖聞覺有異志，使彥宗、斜缽宣慰之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jue was resident commissioner of the Southern Capital; hearing that Jue harbored disloyal intent, Taizu sent Yanzong and Xiebo to console and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue held the southern capital; when Taizu heard he was wavering in loyalty, he dispatched Yanzong and Xiebo to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 太祖至鴛鴦濼，不豫，還上京，留宗翰都統軍事，留彥宗佐之。

translations.literal: When Taizu reached Mandarin Duck Marsh he was unwell, returned to the Supreme Capital, left Zonghan as commander-in-chief of the armies, and left Yanzong to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: At Mandarin Duck Marsh Taizu fell ill, returned to the supreme capital, left Zonghan in overall command of the armies, and had Yanzong assist him.

sentences.zh: 及張覺敗奔于宋，眾推張敦固為都統，殺使者，乘城拒守，攻之不肯下。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jue was defeated and fled to Song, the masses made Zhang Dun'gu commander-in-chief, killed the envoys, manned the walls to resist, and would not yield to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jue was routed and fled to Song, the garrison installed Zhang Dun'gu as commander, killed the envoys, held the walls, and refused to surrender despite repeated assaults.

sentences.zh: 彥宗同中書門下平章事，知樞密院事，加侍中，佐宗望軍。

translations.literal: Yanzong was made Co-Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, head of the Bureau of Military Affairs, additionally made Palace Attendant, and assisted Zongwang's army.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong became co-grand councillor, took charge of military affairs, received the additional title Palace Attendant, and served alongside Zongwang's army.

sentences.zh: 宗望奏，方圖攻取，凡州縣之事委彥宗裁決之。

translations.literal: Zongwang memorialized that he was then planning attacks and entrusted all matters of prefectures and counties to Yanzong's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang reported that he was pressing the campaign and left all civil and military matters in the conquered prefectures to Yanzong's judgment.

sentences.zh: 天會二年，詔彥宗曰：「中京等兩路先多拒命，故遣使撫諭，貰其官民之罪，所犯在降附前者勿論。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhui an edict told Yanzong: "The two circuits including the Central Capital first largely refused orders, so envoys were sent to comfort and instruct them, pardoning the offenses of officials and commoners; crimes committed before submission are not to be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 2 the court instructed Yanzong: "The Central Capital circuit and the other route had largely resisted us, so we are sending envoys to reassure them and pardon officials and civilians alike—nothing done before they submitted will be held against them.

sentences.zh: 卿等選官與使者往諭之，使勤於稼穡。」

translations.literal: You and your colleagues should select officials to go with the envoys to instruct them and make them diligent in farming."
translations.idiomatic: Choose officials to accompany the envoys and urge the people back to their fields.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大舉伐宋，彥宗畫十策，詔彥宗兼領漢軍都統。

translations.literal: Before long a great campaign against Song was mounted; Yanzong drafted ten strategies, and an edict appointed him also commander-in-chief of the Han armies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the court launched a major campaign against Song. Yanzong drew up ten strategic proposals and was ordered to command the Han forces as well.

sentences.zh: 蔡靖以燕山降。

translations.literal: Cai Jing surrendered Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing surrendered the Yanshan region.

sentences.zh: 詔彥宗凡燕京一品以下官皆承制注授，遂進兵伐宋。

translations.literal: An edict directed that Yanzong should appoint by imperial commission all officials of Yanjing from the first rank downward, and the army then advanced against Song.
translations.idiomatic: The court authorized Yanzong to commission all Yanjing officials down to the first rank, after which the army marched south against Song.

sentences.zh: 至汴，宋少帝割地納質，師還。

translations.literal: Reaching Bian, the young Song emperor ceded territory and sent hostages, and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Bian, the young Song emperor ceded land and sent hostages, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宗望分將士屯安肅、雄、霸、廣信之境，留闍母、彥宗于燕京節制諸軍。

translations.literal: Zongwang divided officers and soldiers to garrison the borders of Ansu, Xiong, Ba, and Guangxin, leaving Zhamu and Yanzong at Yanjing to control the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang stationed troops along the Ansu, Xiong, Ba, and Guangxin frontiers and left Zhamu and Yanzong at Yanjing to direct the garrisons.

sentences.zh: 明年，再伐宋，已圍汴京，彥宗謂宗翰、宗望曰：「蕭何入關，秋毫無犯，惟收圖籍。

translations.literal: The next year they campaigned against Song again; already besieging Bianjing, Yanzong said to Zonghan and Zongwang: "When Xiao He entered the passes he did not violate so much as a hair's breadth, but only collected registers and maps.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they invaded Song again. With Bianjing already under siege, Yanzong told Zonghan and Zongwang: "When Xiao He entered the passes he took nothing from the people—only the archives.

sentences.zh: 遼太宗入汴，載路車、法服、石經以歸，皆令則也。」

translations.literal: When the Liao Taizong entered Bian he carried off the imperial carriage, ritual vestments, and stone classics—all models to follow."
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao Taizong took Bian he brought back the imperial carriage, court regalia, and stone classics—all worthy precedents."

sentences.zh: 二帥嘉納之，執二帝以歸。

translations.literal: The two commanders approved his advice and took the two emperors back captive.
translations.idiomatic: Both commanders accepted his counsel and returned with the two Song emperors as captives.

sentences.zh: 天會六年薨，年五十三，追封鄆王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui he died, aged fifty-three, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianhui year 6 at the age of fifty-three and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，例降封開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong, by precedent his enfeoffment was reduced to Grand Master of the Palace with Honored Standing as the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong year 2, following the usual practice, his posthumous rank was reduced to Grand Master of the Palace with Honored Standing as the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 大定十五年，追封兗國公，諡英敏。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Dading he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yan and given the posthumous name Yingmin.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading year 15 he was posthumously made Duke of Yan with the posthumous name Yingmin, meaning Acute and Keen.

sentences.zh: 子萼、筈。

translations.literal: His sons were E and Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were E and Kuo.

sentences.zh: 子 萼

translations.literal: Son E
translations.idiomatic: His son E

sentences.zh: 萼，彥宗季子也。

translations.literal: E was Yanzong's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: E was Yanzong's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 遼末以廕補閣門祗候。

translations.literal: At the end of Liao he entered office by hereditary privilege as a gate attendant of the Imperial Portal.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Liao he received a hereditary appointment as attendant at the Imperial Portal.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年，授禮賓使，累官德州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianfu he was made Master of Ceremonies for Guests and rose through offices to Defender-in-Chief of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu year 7 he was appointed Master of Ceremonies for Guests and eventually became Defender-in-Chief of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 天德初，稍加擢用，曆左右宣徽使，拜參知政事，進尚書左丞，為沁南軍節度使，曆臨洮、太原尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was gradually promoted further, served as Left and Right Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was made Vice Grand Councillor, advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, became military commissioner of the Qinnan Army, and served as prefect of Lintao and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiande reign he rose steadily through the Left and Right Palace Secretariat commissions, became vice grand councillor and then Left Vice Director, held the Qinnan military commission, and governed Lintao and Taiyuan in turn.

sentences.zh: 正隆南伐，為漢南道行營兵馬都統制。

translations.literal: On the southern campaign of Zhenglong he was overall commander of the field headquarters of the Han South Route.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenglong southern campaign he commanded the Han South Route field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 大定初，除興中尹，封任國公，曆順天、定武軍節度使、濟南尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he was made prefect of Xingzhong, enfeoffed as Duke of Ren, and served successively as military commissioner of Shuntian and Dingwu armies and as prefect of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading he became prefect of Xingzhong, was enfeoffed Duke of Ren, and later held the Shuntian and Dingwu military commissions and the Jinan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 萼淫縱無行，所至貪墨狼籍。

translations.literal: E was licentious and unrestrained in conduct; wherever he went his greed and corruption were notorious.
translations.idiomatic: E was dissolute and unrestrained, and everywhere he served he left a trail of corruption.

sentences.zh: 廉使劾之，詔遣大理少卿張九思就濟南鞫問。

translations.literal: The integrity commissioner impeached him, and an edict sent Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Jiusi to Jinan to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: The integrity commissioner brought charges, and the court sent Vice Director Zhang Jiusi of the Court of Judicial Review to Jinan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 既就逮，不測所以，引刃自殺，不死。

translations.literal: Once arrested, unable to foresee his fate, he drew a blade to kill himself but did not die.
translations.idiomatic: After his arrest, dreading what might come, he tried to take his own life but survived.

sentences.zh: 詔削官一階，罷歸田裏，卒。

translations.literal: An edict stripped him of one rank, dismissed him to his home district, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The court reduced his rank by one step, sent him home, and he died there.

sentences.zh: 子仲詢，天德三年，賜王彥潛榜及第。

translations.literal: His son Zhongxun, in the third year of Tiande, was granted graduation on Wang Yanqian's examination list.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongxun passed the examinations in Tiande year 3 on Wang Yanqian's list.

sentences.zh: 子 筈

translations.literal: Son Kuo
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuo

sentences.zh: 筈，彥宗次子。

translations.literal: Kuo was Yanzong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was Yanzong's second son.

sentences.zh: 幼時以廕隸閣門，不就，去從學。

translations.literal: In youth he was enrolled in the Imperial Portal by hereditary privilege but would not take the post and left to pursue study.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was placed in the Imperial Portal by privilege but declined the post and went away to study.

sentences.zh: 遼末調兵，而筈在選中。

translations.literal: At the end of Liao troops were mobilized, and Kuo was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao mobilized troops near the dynasty's end, Kuo was among those drafted.

sentences.zh: 遼兵敗，左右多散亡，乃選筈為扈從，授左承制。

translations.literal: When Liao forces were defeated and many attendants scattered, he was chosen as an escort and made Left Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liao defeat scattered most of the retinue, he was chosen as an escort and appointed Left Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遼主西奔，蕭妃攝政，賜筈進士第，授尚書左司員外郎，寄班閣門。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler fled west; Empress Xiao held regency, granted Kuo the jinshi degree, appointed him Outer Assistant Director of the Left Office of the Department of State Affairs, and attached him to the Imperial Portal roster.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor fled west and Empress Xiao ruled as regent, she granted Kuo the jinshi degree, made him Outer Assistant Director in the Left Office of State Affairs, and attached him to the Imperial Portal.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年，太祖取燕，筈從其父兄出降，遷尚書左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianfu, when Taizu took Yan, Kuo followed his father and elder brothers in surrender and was transferred to Director of the Left Office of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu year 7, when Taizu seized Yan, Kuo surrendered with his father and brothers and was promoted to Director of the Left Office of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 八年，授殿中少監。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，宋，夏遣使吊慰，凡館見禮儀皆筈詳定。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, Song and Xia sent envoys of condolence; Kuo worked out in detail all protocols for reception in the guest houses.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu's death, Song and Western Xia sent condolence missions, and Kuo laid down every detail of the reception ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉少卿，授西上閣門使，仍從事元帥府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, made Commissioner of the Western Upper Imperial Portal, and continued to serve the Marshal's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, Commissioner of the Western Upper Imperial Portal, and continued to serve at the Marshal's Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 元帥府以便宜從事，凡約束廢置及四方號令多從筈之畫焉。

translations.literal: The Marshal's Headquarters acted as circumstances required; most regulations abolished or instituted and proclamations to the four quarters followed Kuo's plans.
translations.idiomatic: The Marshal's Headquarters exercised broad discretion, and most administrative orders and proclamations to the regions followed Kuo's drafting.

sentences.zh: 天會二年，遷太常少卿、東上閣門使，從宗翰伐宋，圍太原。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhui he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Imperial Portal, followed Zonghan in the campaign against Song, and besieged Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 2 he became Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices and Eastern Upper Portal Commissioner, joined Zonghan's campaign against Song, and helped besiege Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉卿，權簽宣徽院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and given acting charge of signing for the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Imperial Stud and given acting authority over the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，授左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Left Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 秋，複南征，權中書省樞密院事。

translations.literal: In autumn he campaigned south again with acting charge of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he joined the southern campaign again with acting authority over the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，明年起複，直樞密院事加給事中。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father; the next year he was recalled to service, made direct administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and additionally given the title Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he mourned, was recalled the next year, took direct charge of military affairs, and received the additional title Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 七年，為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十年，改彰信軍節度使，權簽中書省樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army with acting charge of signing for the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army while retaining acting authority over the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，改左宣徽使，熙宗幸燕，法駕儀仗筈討論者為多。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan he was changed to Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; when Xizong visited Yan, Kuo was largely the one who deliberated on the imperial carriage escort and ceremonial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan year 2 he became Left Palace Secretariat Commissioner; when Emperor Xizong visited Yan, Kuo did most of the planning for the imperial procession and ceremonial regalia.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，充江南封冊使，假中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong he served as envoy to enfeoff the Jiangnan ruler, with acting title of Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year 2 he headed the mission to invest the southern ruler, bearing the acting title Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 既至臨安，而宋人榜其居曰「行宮」，筈曰：「未受命，而名行宮，非也。」

translations.literal: When he reached Lin'an the Song had posted a placard on his lodging reading "Traveling Palace"; Kuo said: "Before credentials have been received, to call it a traveling palace is improper."
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Lin'an he found the Song had labeled his quarters "Traveling Palace." Kuo said: "You have not yet received our commission—calling this a traveling palace is wrong.

sentences.zh: 請去榜而後行禮。

translations.literal: He asked that the placard be removed before ceremonies were performed.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted the placard be removed before any ceremony could proceed.

sentences.zh: 宋人驚服其有識，欲厚賄說之，奉金珠三十余萬，而筈不之顧，皆歎曰：「大國有人焉。」

translations.literal: The Song were startled and admired his discernment; wishing to win him over with rich bribes they presented more than three hundred thousand in gold and pearls, but Kuo paid no heed, and all sighed: "The great state has its men."
translations.idiomatic: The Song were astonished by his judgment and tried to win him with lavish gifts—more than three hundred thousand in gold and pearls—but Kuo would not look at them, and people exclaimed: "The great power truly has men of caliber."

sentences.zh: 六年，為行台尚書右丞相，兼判左宣徽使事，留京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Right Grand Councillor of the Branch Secretariat of the Department of State Affairs, additionally supervising the Left Palace Secretariat, and remained at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became Right Grand Councillor of the Branch Secretariat, also supervised the Left Palace Secretariat, and remained at the capital.

sentences.zh: 或請厘革河南官吏之濫雜者，筈曰：「廢齊用兵江表，求一切近效，其所用人不必皆以章程，故有不由科目而為大吏，不試弓馬而握兵柄者。

translations.literal: Some asked to reform the mixed abuses among officials south of the Yellow River; Kuo said: "When the Qi state was abolished and troops were used on the Jiang tables, immediate results were sought; those employed need not all have followed regulations, so some became high officials without the examination curriculum and some held military authority without bow-and-horse tests.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed cleaning up the confused official ranks south of the Yellow River, Kuo said: "When Qi was abolished and we campaigned along the Yangtze, we needed quick results. Not everyone was appointed by the book—some rose to high office without passing the examinations, and some held military command without archery and riding tests.

sentences.zh: 今撫定未久，姑收人心，奈何為是紛更也。」

translations.literal: Pacification is not yet long established; for now we should win hearts—why make such repeated changes."
translations.idiomatic: Pacification is still fresh—we should win people's loyalty. Why stir up so much turmoil now.

sentences.zh: 遂仍其舊。

translations.literal: The former arrangements were therefore kept.
translations.idiomatic: The old arrangements were left in place.

sentences.zh: 七年，帥府議于館陶築三城，以為有警即令北軍入居之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the marshal's headquarters proposed building three walled towns at Guantao so that in an emergency northern troops could enter and occupy them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year headquarters proposed building three fortified towns at Guantao so northern troops could move inside at the first alarm.

sentences.zh: 筈曰：「今天下一家，孰為南北。

translations.literal: Kuo said: "Today all under Heaven is one family—who is north and who is south.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo said: "The realm is one family now—who is still north and who south.

sentences.zh: 設或有變，軍人入城，獨能安耶。

translations.literal: If there should be trouble, soldiers entering the towns—can they alone be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: If trouble came, would the townsfolk feel safe with soldiers pouring into their walls.

sentences.zh: 當嚴武備以察奸，無示彼此之間也。」

translations.literal: We should tighten military readiness to detect treachery and not display a sense of division between us."
translations.idiomatic: Keep defenses sharp to watch for malice, but do not advertise a split between us."

sentences.zh: 其後，竟從筈議。

translations.literal: In the end they followed Kuo's view.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they adopted Kuo's advice.

sentences.zh: 初，以河外三州賜夏人，或言秦之在夏者數千人，皆願來歸。

translations.literal: Earlier the three prefectures west of the river had been granted to the Xia; some said several thousand Qin people in Xia all wished to return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had granted the three prefectures west of the Yellow River to Western Xia; some reported that several thousand Qin people living in Xia wished to come back.

sentences.zh: 諸將請約之，筈曰：「三小州不足為輕重，恐失朝廷大信。

translations.literal: The generals asked to arrange it; Kuo said: "Three small prefectures are not worth the weight—there is fear of losing the court's great trust.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to arrange their return, but Kuo said: "Three small prefectures are not worth the gamble—we would risk the court's credibility.

sentences.zh: 且秦人之在蜀者倍多於此，何獨舍彼而取此乎。」

translations.literal: Moreover Qin people in Shu are more than twice as many as this—why abandon those and take these."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, there are more than twice as many Qin people in Shu—why abandon them and take only these.

sentences.zh: 遂從筈議。

translations.literal: They then followed Kuo's view.
translations.idiomatic: They followed Kuo's view.

sentences.zh: 陝西邊帥請完沿邊城郭以備南寇，筈曰：「我利車騎而不利城守。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi frontier commander asked to complete the border walled towns against southern raiders; Kuo said: "We profit from chariots and cavalry and do not profit from holding walled towns.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi frontier commander asked to repair border fortifications against southern raids. Kuo said: "We rely on cavalry, not on walled defense.

sentences.zh: 今城之，則勞民而結怨。

translations.literal: If we fortify them now, we will weary the people and breed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Building them up now would exhaust the people and breed resentment.

sentences.zh: 況盟已定，豈可妄動。」

translations.literal: Moreover the alliance is already settled—how can we act rashly."
translations.idiomatic: The treaty is already in place—how can we stir things up recklessly.

sentences.zh: 遂罷之。

translations.literal: The project was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 子 仲誨

translations.literal: Son Zhonghui
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhonghui

sentences.zh: 仲誨字子忠。

translations.literal: Zhonghui, courtesy name Zizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui, whose courtesy name was Zizhong.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，以宰相子授忠勇校尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong, as a grand councillor's son he was made Captain of Loyal Valor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangtong, as a grand councillor's son, he was appointed Captain of Loyal Valor.

sentences.zh: 九年，賜進士第，除應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was granted the jinshi degree and made Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he received the jinshi degree and became an attendant scribe in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 海陵嚴暴，臣下應對多失次。

translations.literal: Hailing was severe and violent; subordinates often lost composure in answering him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was harsh and violent, and officials often faltered when answering him.

sentences.zh: 嘗以時政訪問在朝官，仲誨從容敷奏，無懼色，海陵稱賞之。

translations.literal: Once he questioned court officials on current affairs; Zhonghui answered at ease without fear, and Hailing praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he questioned court officials on current affairs; Zhonghui replied calmly without fear, and Hailing praised him.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，丁父憂，起複翰林修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he entered mourning for his father, was recalled to service, and made Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan, after his father's death, he was recalled from mourning and made Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，遷待制，尋兼修起居注、左補闕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was transferred to Attendant Drafter, and soon additionally compiled the Diary of Activity and Attendance and served as Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading year 2 he became Attendant Drafter and soon also compiled the imperial diary and served as Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔仲誨與左司員外郎蒲察蒲速越廉問所過州縣，仲誨等還奏狀，詔玉田縣令李方進一階，順州知法、權密雲縣事王宗永擢密雲縣尉，順州司候張璘、密雲縣尉石抹烏者皆免去。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict sent Zhonghui with Outer Assistant Director of the Left Office Pucha Pusuyue to conduct integrity inquiries in the prefectures and counties they passed through; when Zhonghui and the others returned and memorialized, an edict advanced Yutian magistrate Li Fang one rank, promoted Shunzhou legal officer and acting Miyun county affairs Wang Zongyong to Miyun county captain, and dismissed Shunzhou judicial assistant Zhang Lin and Miyun county captain Shimowu Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the court sent Zhonghui with Pucha Pusuyue of the Left Office to inspect integrity in the prefectures they visited. On their return, Yutian magistrate Li Fang was promoted one rank, Wang Zongyong of Shunzhou was made Miyun county captain, and Zhang Lin and Shimowu Zhe were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複太子右諭德，遷翰林直學士、改棣州防禦使。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother, was recalled to service as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance, and changed to Defender-in-Chief of Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he was recalled as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, became Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance, and was transferred to Defender-in-Chief of Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 厭次縣捕得強盜數十人，詣州欲以全獲希賞。

translations.literal: Yanci county arrested several tens of bandits and brought them to the prefecture hoping to win reward for capturing them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yanci county arrested several dozen bandits and brought them to the prefecture hoping for a reward for a full roundup.

sentences.zh: 仲誨疑其有冤，緩其獄。

translations.literal: Zhonghui suspected some were wrongly accused and slowed the case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui suspected wrongful convictions and slowed the proceedings.

sentences.zh: 同僚曰：「縣境多盜，請置之法，以懲其餘。」

translations.literal: Colleagues said: "The county has many bandits; please punish them by law to warn the rest."
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues urged: "The county is overrun with bandits—execute them under the law to deter the rest.

sentences.zh: 仲誨乃擇老稚者先釋之。

translations.literal: Zhonghui then chose the old and young to release first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui instead selected the elderly and children for release first.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乃獲真盜。

translations.literal: Before long the real bandits were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the real culprits were caught.

sentences.zh: 入為禮部侍郎兼左諭德，遷太子詹事兼左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and was transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Vice Director of Rites and Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Left Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「東宮官屬，尤當選用正人，如行檢不修及不稱位者，具以名聞。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Eastern Palace staff especially should be upright men; those whose conduct is not cultivated or who are unfit for their posts—report their names in full.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Eastern Palace staff must be men of integrity. Report by name anyone whose conduct is lax or who is unfit for his post.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「東宮講書或論議間，當以孝儉德行正身之事告之。」

translations.literal: He also said: "When lecturing or debating in the Eastern Palace, tell him of filial piety, frugality, virtue, and correcting the person."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "In lectures or discussions at the Eastern Palace, teach him filial piety, frugality, virtue, and self-discipline."

sentences.zh: 頃之，東宮請增牧人及張設什用，上謂仲誨曰：「太子生於富貴，每教之恭儉。

translations.literal: Before long the Eastern Palace asked to increase herdsmen and expand furnishings; the emperor told Zhonghui: "The crown prince was born to wealth; teach him respect and frugality at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Eastern Palace requested more herdsmen and furnishings. The emperor told Zhonghui: "The crown prince was born to privilege—keep teaching him modesty and thrift.

sentences.zh: 朕服禦未嘗妄有增益，卿以此意諭之。」

translations.literal: I have never rashly added to my robes; convey this meaning to him."
translations.idiomatic: I have never indulged my wardrobe without cause—make that clear to him.

sentences.zh: 改御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年，為宋國歲元使，宋主欲變親起接書之儀，遣館伴王抃來議，曲辨強說，欲要以必從。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he served as envoy for Song's New Year tribute; the Song ruler wished to change the ceremony of rising in person to receive the letter, and sent guest companion Wang Bian to negotiate, arguing roundly and insistently to force compliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he headed the New Year's mission to Song. The Song ruler wanted to alter the ceremony so the emperor would rise in person to receive the letter, and sent Wang Bian as host to argue insistently until Jin yielded.

sentences.zh: 仲誨曰：「使臣奉命，遠來修好，固欲成禮，而信約所載，非使臣輒敢變更。

translations.literal: Zhonghui said: "The envoy received his commission and came from afar to renew amity; he surely wishes to complete the rites, but what the sworn agreement records is not something the envoy may rashly change.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui replied: "I came on orders from afar to renew friendship and wish only to complete the rites. What our treaty records is not mine to alter on my own authority.

sentences.zh: 公等宋國腹心，毋僥倖一時，失大國歡。」

translations.literal: You are the trusted core of Song—do not gamble on the moment and forfeit the great state's goodwill."
translations.idiomatic: You are the heart of Song's government—do not gamble on a moment's advantage and lose the great power's goodwill.

sentences.zh: 往復再三，竟用舊儀，親起接書成禮而還。

translations.literal: After repeated exchanges the old ceremony was used; the ruler rose in person to receive the letter, the rites were completed, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated exchanges the old ceremony stood. The Song emperor rose to receive the letter in person, the rites were completed, and Zhonghui returned.

sentences.zh: 複為太子詹事，遷吏部尚書，轉太子少師兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He again became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and changed to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then Director of Personnel, and finally Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent with the additional post of Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 坐失糾舉大長公主事，與侍御史李瑜各削一階。

translations.literal: He was punished for failing to impeach the Grand Princess; he and Attending Censor Li Yu each had one rank stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted for failing to impeach the Grand Princess; he and Attending Censor Li Yu each lost one rank.

sentences.zh: 仲誨前後為東宮官且十五年，多進規戒，顯宗特加禮敬。

translations.literal: Zhonghui had served as an Eastern Palace official for about fifteen years in all, often offering admonitions; Emperor Xianzong showed him special respect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui had served in the Eastern Palace for some fifteen years in all, offering many admonitions, and Emperor Xianzong treated him with special deference.

sentences.zh: 大定十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Dading he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Dading year 19.

sentences.zh: 仲誨立朝峻整，容色莊重，世宗嘗曰：「朕見劉仲誨嘗若將切諫者。」

translations.literal: Zhonghui was stern and ordered at court, his bearing grave; Emperor Shizong once said: "When I see Liu Zhonghui it is as if he is about to offer a sharp remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui was austere and composed at court, his bearing solemn. Emperor Shizong once said: "Whenever I see Liu Zhonghui, he looks ready to deliver a blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 其以剛嚴見知如此。

translations.literal: Thus he was known for stern integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his reputation for stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 頍字元矩。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Yuanju.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, whose courtesy name was Yuanju.

sentences.zh: 以大臣子孫充閣門祗候，調莘縣令，召為承奉班都知，遷西上閣門副使兼宮苑令，累遷西上、東上閣門使。

translations.literal: As a minister's descendant he served as Imperial Portal attendant, was transferred to magistrate of Xin county, summoned as Director of the Service Class, promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Western Upper Imperial Portal and Park of the Palace Domestic Service, and rose through Western and Eastern Upper Imperial Portal Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As a minister's grandson he served as an Imperial Portal attendant, became magistrate of Xin county, was summoned as Director of the Service Class, and rose to Vice Commissioner of the Western Upper Portal and Park of the Palace Domestic Service, then to commissioner of both the Western and Eastern Upper Portals.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年，宋盱眙軍報：明年賀正旦使魯 <宜宜>、楊明輝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe the Song Xuyi army reported: next year's New Year's congratulatory envoys Lu Yi and Yang Minghui.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 2 the Song post at Xuyi reported that the next New Year's envoys would be Lu Yi and Yang Minghui.

sentences.zh: 及過界，副使乃王處久。

translations.literal: When they crossed the border the vice envoy was Wang Chujiu.
translations.idiomatic: When they crossed the border, however, the vice envoy was Wang Chujiu.

sentences.zh: 入見，魯<宜宜>殿上不雙跪。

translations.literal: On entering audience Lu Yi did not perform the double kneel in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Lu Yi failed to perform the double kneel in the hall.

sentences.zh: 詔<宜宜>就閣詰問先報名銜楊明輝不復報改王處久之故，及不雙跪者。

translations.literal: An edict had Lu Yi questioned at the Pavilion on why Yang Minghui was first reported but not re-reported when changed to Wang Chujiu, and on the failure to double kneel.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Lu Yi to the Pavilion to explain why Yang Minghui had been announced but Wang Chujiu was not reported in his place, and why he had not double-kneeled.

sentences.zh: 魯<宜宜>對，拜時並雙跪，有足疾似單跪者。

translations.literal: Lu Yi answered that when bowing he performed both kneels; he had a foot ailment that made it seem a single kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi replied that he had knelt on both knees when bowing, but a foot ailment made it appear he had knelt on only one.

sentences.zh: 初，南苑有唐舊碑，書「貞元十年御史大夫劉怦葬」。

translations.literal: Earlier in the Southern Park there was an old Tang stele reading "Burial of Censor-in-Chief Liu Bing, tenth year of Zhenyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a Tang stele in the Southern Park read: "Burial of Censor-in-Chief Liu Bing, Zhenyuan year 10."

sentences.zh: 上見之曰：「苑中不宜有墓。」

translations.literal: The emperor seeing it said: "There should not be a tomb in the park."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said on seeing it: "A park should not contain a tomb.

sentences.zh: 頍家本怦後，詔賜頍錢三百貫改葬之。

translations.literal: Yi's family were descendants of Bing; an edict gave Yi three hundred strings of cash to rebury him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's family were descendants of Bing, and the court granted Yi three hundred strings of cash to move the grave.

sentences.zh: 三遷右宣徽使。

translations.literal: He was transferred three times to Right Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times to Right Palace Secretariat Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，轉左宣徽使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred to Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou year 2 he became Left Palace Secretariat Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，致仕，遷一官。

translations.literal: The next year he retired; his office was advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired and received a one-rank promotion in title.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿舊人也，今朝廷多故，豈宜去位。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are an old associate; the court has many troubles—how can you leave your post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You are an old servant, and the court faces many troubles—how can you leave your post now.

sentences.zh: 朕自東宮薨後，思慮不周，俟稍寧息，即以上郡處卿。」

translations.literal: Since the Eastern Palace's bereavement my thoughts have not been thorough; when things calm somewhat I shall place you in an upper prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Since the crown prince's death my mind has not been settled. When things calm I shall give you an upper prefecture.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起為知開封府。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled to serve as prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 四年正月元日，攝左宣徽使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of the fourth reign cycle, on New Year's Day, he acted as Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day in the first month of the fourth year he acted as Left Palace Secretariat Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 再請老，未半歲複起為御史中丞。

translations.literal: He again requested retirement; before half a year had passed he was again recalled as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to retire, but within half a year was recalled as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 詔安撫河南路，捕盜賊。

translations.literal: An edict sent him to pacify the Henan circuit and capture bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered him to pacify the Henan circuit and hunt down bandits.

sentences.zh: 坐與保靜軍節度使會飲，解職。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for drinking with the military commissioner of Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office for drinking with the military commissioner of the Baojing Army.

sentences.zh: 起為太子詹事，遷太子少師。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and transferred to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 詹事院欲辟廣東宮周牆，頍請于皇太子曰：「師旅饑饉之際，何為興此役。」

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent's household wished to expand the eastern palace walls; Yi asked the crown prince: "At a time of armies and famine, why raise this project."
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent's office wished to enlarge the eastern palace walls. Yi asked the crown prince: "In a time of war and famine, why undertake this work.

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: It was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The project was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 時立愛

translations.literal: Shi Liai
translations.idiomatic: Shi Liai

sentences.zh: 時立愛，字昌壽，涿州新城人。

translations.literal: Shi Liai, courtesy name Changshou, was a native of Xincheng in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Liai, whose courtesy name was Changshou, came from Xincheng in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 父承謙，以財雄鄉里，歲饑發倉廩賑貧乏，假貸者與之折券。

translations.literal: His father Chengqian was wealthy in the countryside; in years of famine he opened granaries to relieve the poor and tore up the IOUs of those who borrowed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengqian was the wealthiest man in the district; in famine years he opened his granaries to feed the poor and burned the IOUs of those who owed him.

sentences.zh: 遼太康九年，中進士第，調泰州幕官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Liao Taikang he passed the jinshi and was assigned as staff officer of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Liao Taikang year 9 he passed the jinshi examinations and was posted as staff officer of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，調同知春州事。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father; when mourning ended he was assigned as Associate Prefect of Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death and mourning he was assigned as associate prefect of Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 未逾年，遷雲內縣令，再除文德令。

translations.literal: Before a year had passed he was transferred to magistrate of Yunnei, then again appointed magistrate of Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he became magistrate of Yunnei, then was appointed magistrate of Wende.

sentences.zh: 樞密院選為吏房副都承旨，轉都承旨。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs selected him as Deputy Director of the Personnel Section, then Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs chose him as deputy director of the personnel section, then as director.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史中丞，剛正敢言，忤權貴。

translations.literal: He rose to Censor-in-Chief, upright and outspoken, offending the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Censor-in-Chief, upright and outspoken, and offended powerful men.

sentences.zh: 除燕京副留守，丁母憂，起復舊職，遷遼興軍節度使兼漢軍都統。

translations.literal: He was made Vice Resident Commissioner of Yanjing; he entered mourning for his mother, was recalled to his old post, and transferred to military commissioner of Liaoxing Army and commander-in-chief of Han forces.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice resident commissioner of Yanjing; after his mother's death he was recalled from mourning to his old post, then became military commissioner of the Liaoxing Army and commander-in-chief of the Han forces.

sentences.zh: 太祖已定燕京，訪求得平州人韓詢持詔招諭平州。

translations.literal: When Taizu had pacified Yanjing he sought out the Pingzhou man Han Xun to hold an edict and summon Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu secured Yanjing he found a man of Pingzhou named Han Xun and sent him with an edict to summon that region.

sentences.zh: 是時，奚王回離保在盧能嶺，立愛未敢即朝見，先使人來送款曰：「民情愚執，不即順從，願降寬恩，以慰反側。」

translations.literal: At that time the Xi king Huilibao was at Luneng Ridge; Liai did not dare at once to appear at court, but first sent a man with his submission saying: "The people's minds are foolishly stubborn and did not at once submit; grant lenient favor to comfort those wavering."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xi king Huilibao was at Luneng Ridge. Liai did not dare present himself at court immediately, but first sent a messenger with his submission: "The people are stubborn and did not submit at once. Grant them leniency to calm their fears.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕親巡西土，底定全燕，號令所加，城邑皆下。

translations.literal: An edict said: "I personally tour the western regions and have settled all Yan; where commands reach, walled towns submit.
translations.idiomatic: The reply edict said: "I have personally toured the west and settled all of Yan; wherever my command reaches, cities submit.

sentences.zh: 爰嘉忠款，特示優恩，應在彼大小官員可皆充舊職，諸囚禁配隸並從釋免。」

translations.literal: Loving your loyal submission, special favor is shown; all officials great and small there may retain their old posts, and all prisoners and assigned persons are released."
translations.idiomatic: In reward for your loyal submission I show special favor: all officials there may keep their posts, and all prisoners and conscripts are released.

sentences.zh: 於是，遼帝尚在天德，平州雖降，民心未固。

translations.literal: Then the Liao emperor was still at Tiande; though Pingzhou had surrendered, hearts were not yet firm.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor was still at Tiande; though Pingzhou had surrendered, the people's loyalty was not yet secure.

sentences.zh: 奚王回離保軍所在保聚，薊州已降複叛。

translations.literal: The Xi king Huilibao's forces gathered at their strongholds; Jizhou had surrendered but rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi king Huilibao's troops gathered in their strongholds, and Jizhou, though it had surrendered, rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 民間流言謂：「金人所下城邑，始則存撫，後則俘掠。」

translations.literal: Popular rumor said: "In walled towns taken by the Jin, first they soothe, later they plunder."
translations.idiomatic: Rumor among the people ran: "In every city the Jin take, they soothe at first and plunder afterward.

sentences.zh: 時立愛雖開諭而不肯信，乃上表：「乞下明詔，遣官分行郡邑，宣諭德義。

translations.literal: Though Liai explained this, they would not believe; he memorialized: "I beg an explicit edict dispatching officials through the prefectures to proclaim virtuous justice.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liai explained this, they would not believe him, and he memorialized: "I beg a clear edict sending officials through the prefectures to proclaim the court's benevolence.

sentences.zh: 他日兵臨于宋，順則撫之，逆則討之，兵不勞而天下定矣。」

translations.literal: When troops later reach Song, if they submit then soothe them, if they resist then punish them—the realm will be settled without exhausting the armies."
translations.idiomatic: When armies later reach Song, soothe those who submit and punish those who resist, and the realm will be settled without exhausting our forces.

sentences.zh: 上覽表嘉之，詔答曰：「卿始率吏民歸附，複條利害，悉合朕意，嘉歎不忘。

translations.literal: The emperor reading the memorial approved and answered: "You first led officials and people to submit and set forth advantages and harms, all agreeing with my intent; my praise does not fade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with approval and replied: "You first led officials and people to submit, and your analysis of advantage and harm fully accords with my intent. My praise does not fade.

sentences.zh: 山西部族緣遼主未獲，恐陰相連結，故遷處於嶺東。

translations.literal: The Shanxi tribal groups because the Liao ruler was not yet captured feared secret connection, so they were moved east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal groups west of the mountains, fearing secret ties while the Liao ruler was still at large, were moved east of the ranges.

sentences.zh: 西京人民既無異望，皆按堵如故。

translations.literal: The Western Capital people had no other intent and all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Western Capital harbored no disloyal intent and lived as before.

sentences.zh: 或有將卒貪悍，冒犯紀律，輒掠降人者。

translations.literal: Some soldiers were greedy and fierce, violating discipline and plundering those who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Some soldiers were greedy and violent, broke discipline, and plundered those who had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 已諭諸部及軍帥，約束兵士，秋毫有犯，必刑無赦。

translations.literal: The various departments and army commanders have been instructed to restrain the troops; the slightest violation will be punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: I have instructed all departments and commanders to restrain the troops: the slightest offense will be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 今遣斡羅阿裏等為卿副貳，以撫斯民，其告諭所部，使知朕意。」

translations.literal: Now Woluo Ari and others are sent as your deputies to soothe this people; proclaim to your districts so they know my mind."
translations.idiomatic: I now send Woluo Ari and others as your deputies to reassure the people. Proclaim this to your districts so they know my intent."

sentences.zh: 其後，以平州為南京，用張覺為留守，時立愛遂去平州。

translations.literal: Later Pingzhou was made the Southern Capital, Zhang Jue made resident commissioner, and Liai then left Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Pingzhou was made the Southern Capital with Zhang Jue as resident commissioner, and Liai left Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 而張覺遂因燕京人東徙，其眾怨望，覺遂叛入于宋。

translations.literal: Zhang Jue then because people of Yanjing moved east, their masses were resentful, and Jue rebelled and entered Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue, resentful over the forced eastward relocation of Yanjing people, rebelled and fled to Song.

sentences.zh: 立愛既去平州歸鄉里，太祖以燕、薊與宋，新城入于宋。

translations.literal: Liai having left Pingzhou returned home; Taizu gave Yan and Ji to Song, and Xincheng came under Song.
translations.idiomatic: Liai returned home from Pingzhou; Taizu ceded Yan and Ji to Song, and Xincheng fell under Song control.

sentences.zh: 宋累詔立愛，立愛見宋政日壞，不肯起，戒其宗族不得求仕。

translations.literal: Song repeatedly issued an edict Liai; Liai saw Song government daily worsening and would not rise; he warned his clan not to seek office.
translations.idiomatic: Song repeatedly summoned Liai, but he saw Song government growing worse daily and refused to serve, warning his clan not to seek office.

sentences.zh: 韓企先

translations.literal: Han Qixian
translations.idiomatic: Han Qixian

sentences.zh: 初，太祖定燕京，始用漢官宰相賞左企弓等，置中書省、樞密院于廣寧府，而朝廷宰相自用女直官號。

translations.literal: When Taizu first pacified Yanjing he began using Han officials as grand chancellors such as Zuo Qigong, establishing the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs at Guangning prefecture, while the court grand chancellors still used Jurchen titles.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first secured Yanjing he began appointing Han officials such as Zuo Qigong as grand chancellors and set up the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs at Guangning, while the central court still used Jurchen titles for its chancellors.

sentences.zh: 太宗初年，無所改更。

translations.literal: In Taizong's early years nothing was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's early reign nothing was changed.

sentences.zh: 及張敦固伏誅，移置中書、樞密于平州，蔡靖以燕山降，移置燕京，凡漢地選授調發租稅皆承制行之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun'gu was executed the Secretariat and Bureau were moved to Pingzhou; when Cai Jing surrendered Yanshan they were moved to Yanjing; all appointments, deployments, and tax collection in Han territories were carried out by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Dun'gu was executed the Secretariat and Bureau moved to Pingzhou; when Cai Jing surrendered Yanshan they moved to Yanjing. All appointments, deployments, and tax collection in Han territories were carried out by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 故自時立愛、劉彥宗及企先輩，官為宰相，其職大抵如此。

translations.literal: Thus from Liai, Liu Yanzong, and Qixian's generation, though titled grand chancellors their duties were largely such.
translations.idiomatic: Thus from the generation of Liai, Liu Yanzong, and Qixian onward, though titled grand chancellors, their duties were largely of this kind.

sentences.zh: 斜也、宗幹當國，勸太宗改女直舊制，用漢官制度。

translations.literal: Xieye and Zonggan held the state and urged Taizong to change old Jurchen institutions and use Han official systems.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye and Zonggan held power and urged Taizong to replace Jurchen custom with Han bureaucratic institutions.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，始定官制，立尚書省以下諸司府寺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui the official system was first fixed, establishing the Department of State Affairs and the various bureaus, offices, and temples below.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 4 the official system was first codified, establishing the Department of State Affairs and the bureaus, offices, and temples beneath it.

sentences.zh: 十年，司空李德固孫引慶求襲其祖猛安，世宗曰：「德固無功，其猛安且闕之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Minister of Works Li Deguo's grandson Yinqing sought to inherit his grandfather's commander rank; the emperor said: "Deguo had no merit; his commander rank shall remain vacant for now.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Li Deguo's grandson Yinqing sought to inherit his grandfather's commander rank. The emperor said: "Deguo earned no merit; let that command remain vacant for now.

sentences.zh: 漢人宰相惟韓企先最賢，他不及也。」

translations.literal: Among Han grand chancellors only Han Qixian was most worthy; the others did not equal him."
translations.idiomatic: Among Han grand chancellors only Han Qixian was truly worthy; none of the others matched him.

sentences.zh: 十一年，將圖功臣像于衍慶宮，上曰：「丞相企先，本朝典章制度多出斯人之手，至於關決大政，與大臣謀議，不使外人知之，由是無人能知其功。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year they were to paint meritorious officials' portraits in the Yansqing Palace; the emperor said: "Grand Councillor Qixian—many of this dynasty's statutes came from this man's hand; in deciding great affairs he deliberated with ministers and would not let outsiders know, so no one could know his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year they planned to paint meritorious officials' portraits in the Yansqing Palace. The emperor said: "Grand Councillor Qixian drafted much of this dynasty's law and institutions. In great affairs he deliberated with ministers in secret, so no one could measure his achievement.

sentences.zh: 前後漢人宰相無能及者，置功臣畫像中，亦足以示勸後人。」

translations.literal: No Han grand councillor before or after could equal him; placing his portrait among meritorious ministers is enough to admonish later men."
translations.idiomatic: No Han grand councillor before or after could equal him. Placing his portrait among the meritorious ministers is enough to admonish those who come after.

sentences.zh: 十五年，諡簡懿。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was given the posthumous name Jianyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he received the posthumous name Jianyi, meaning Simple and Virtuous.

sentences.zh: 子 鐸

translations.literal: Son Duo
translations.idiomatic: His son Duo

sentences.zh: 韓鐸字振文，企先次子也。

translations.literal: Han Duo, courtesy name Zhenwen, was Qixian's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Han Duo, whose courtesy name was Zhenwen, was Qixian's second son.

sentences.zh: 皇統末，以大臣子授武義將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Huangtong, as a minister's son he was made General of Martial Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Huangtong, as a minister's son he was appointed General of Martial Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 熙宗聞其有儒學，賜進士第，除宣徽判官。

translations.literal: Xizong hearing he had Confucian learning granted him the jinshi degree and made him Judge of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong heard of his learning in the Confucian classics, he granted Duo the jinshi degree and made him a judge of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 再遷刑部員外郎，海陵遣中使諭之曰：「郎官，高選也。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Outer Director of the Ministry of Punishments; Hailing sent a palace envoy to instruct him: "A bureau director is a high selection.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Outer Director of the Ministry of Punishments. Hailing sent a palace envoy to tell him: "A bureau directorship is a high appointment.

sentences.zh: 汝勳賢之子，行已蒞官，能世其家，故以命汝。

translations.literal: You are the son of a meritorious worthy; your conduct has already reached office and can carry on the family, so you are appointed.
translations.idiomatic: You are the son of a meritorious minister; your conduct already befits office and can carry on your family line, and that is why you are appointed.

sentences.zh: 苟能夙夜在公，當不次擢用，雖公相可到。」

translations.literal: If you can be diligent from dawn to dusk in public affairs, you will be promoted out of turn—even grand councillor is attainable."
translations.idiomatic: If you serve diligently day and night, you will be promoted out of turn—even the rank of grand councillor is within reach.

sentences.zh: 鐸感奮，獄或有疑，據經議讞。

translations.literal: Duo was stirred; when cases had doubts he deliberated on statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was deeply moved. When cases were doubtful he deliberated according to the classics and statutes.

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，改兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: On Hailing's campaign against Song he was changed to Outer Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: During Hailing's campaign against Song he was transferred to Outer Director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 大定初，遷本部郎中，累官河州防禦使，求養親，解去。

translations.literal: Early in Dading he was transferred to Director in the same ministry, rose to Defender-in-Chief of Hezhou, and requested leave to support his parents and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading he became Director in the same ministry, rose to Defender-in-Chief of Hezhou, then asked leave to care for his parents and resigned.

sentences.zh: 召為左諫議大夫，遷中都路都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Remonstrating Grand Master and transferred to Commissioner of Transport for the Central Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Left Remonstrating Grand Master and made Commissioner of Transport for the Central Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上謂宰臣曰：「韓鐸年高，不任繁劇，且其母老矣，可與之便郡。」

translations.literal: Before long the emperor told the councillors: "Han Duo is aged and cannot bear heavy duties; moreover his mother is old—give him a convenient prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor told his councillors: "Han Duo is advanced in years and cannot bear heavy duties, and his mother is old—give him a convenient prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於是改順天軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was therefore changed to military commissioner of Shuntian Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made military commissioner of the Shuntian Army.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：太祖入燕，始用遼南、北面官僚制度。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When Taizu entered Yan he first used the Liao southern and northern bureaucratic systems.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: When Taizu entered Yan he first adopted the Liao southern and northern bureaucratic systems.

sentences.zh: 是故劉彥宗、時立愛規為施設，不見於朝廷之上。

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Yanzong and Shi Liai planned and implemented arrangements not seen at the court level.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Liu Yanzong and Shi Liai planned and carried out measures that did not appear at the central court.

sentences.zh: 軍旅之暇，治官政，庀民事，務農積穀，內供京師，外給轉餉，此其功也。

translations.literal: In intervals between campaigns they governed civil administration and arranged civilian affairs, promoted farming and stored grain, supplying the capital within and transport without—this was their achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals between campaigns they governed civil affairs, settled the people, promoted farming and stored grain, supplied the capital within and transport without—this was their achievement.

sentences.zh: 韓企先入相兩朝，幾二十年，成功著業，世宗稱其賢焉。

translations.literal: Han Qixian first served as grand chancellor through two reigns for nearly twenty years, achieved merit and established his work, and Emperor Shizong praised his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qixian had served as grand chancellor through two reigns for nearly twenty years, leaving a record of solid achievement, and Emperor Shizong praised his excellence.
